#### Expert Systems Tab

Expert system validations use statistical analysis of historical data to identify uncharacteristic changes in a meter's data flow pattern. A valid range of lower and upper bounds is calculated using a running or weighted average of previous records. Specify the number of previous records used for this average using the field in the upper right corner of the Expert Systems tab.

If a value in a record being imported falls outside of this range, an exception will be generated.

If the specified date range does not contain values for the main data point (volume for volumetric calculation method; mass for mass calculation method), set points will not be calculated for the meter and will not be set in the Meter Editor. If values are not provided for the Average Count and Step fields, default values are used to calculate set points.

<div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Set Dead Band Factors">

To prevent excessive exceptions resulting from set points that are too tight, you can specify a dead band. Click the **Set** button to access the Dead Band screen.

The dead band calculation for Expert Systems validations varies depending on whether percent difference or standard deviation is to be used for generation of exceptions.

<div class="procedure">

To perform the calculation:

1.  In both cases, appropriate values are calculated for the field (DP, pressure, volume, etc.) for the given percentage to be flagged.
2.  If dead band values are to be ignored, no further calculations are needed, and the numbers in step 1 will be used; otherwise, otherwise, one of the following methods will be used:
    - For **standard deviation**, the value calculated in step 1 is multiplied by 1 + the dead band factor entered.
    - For **percent difference**, the value calculated in step 1 is multiplied by the dead band factor entered.

    <div class="example">

    Example 1:

    In step 1, percent difference is used for DP, with a dead band factor of 1.2. A value of 52.4 is calculated. Multiplying 52.4 by 1.2 yields 62.88. That resulting value would be stored in the database.

    Example 2:

    In step 1, standard deviation is used for volume, with a dead band factor of 0.05. A value of 4.8 is calculated. Multiplying 4.8 by 1 + 0.05 yields 5.04. That resulting value would be stored in the database.

    </div>

</div>
